description: Paste the `tools/list` response of an MCP server — yours, or a third party's you are evaluating whether to install — and check its catalogue quality: missing descriptions or annotations, a tool name that suggests it writes or deletes while its annotations say otherwise, context cost per tool (real BPE tokenization), and whether the top-level `instructions` field is set and fits under the ~2 KB some Tool Search clients trim. Add `serverJson`/`packageJson` to also catch the official MCP registry's own field-length and namespace-pattern limits, and a version mismatch between the two — the exact 422/403/400 errors this project hit publishing its own packages. This is NOT an access-security review: it does not evaluate what the tools are permitted to do, only how the catalogue is described. Add `approvedToolsListJson` (the tools/list you reviewed and approved earlier) to catch a "rug pull": tools added or removed since, descriptions that changed or gained poisoning signals, new parameters, and annotations that became less cautious.

approvedToolsListJson.description: The tools/list you approved earlier, to diff against today's

encoding.description: BPE encoding for the token-cost measurement

instructions.description: The server-level `instructions` string, if you have it

packageJson.description: package.json, to cross-check its version against server.json

serverJson.description: The registry manifest (server.json), to check its own limits

toolsListJson.description: The `tools/list` response, either `{"tools": [...]}` or the bare array

name: mcp_catalog_audit
title: Audit an MCP server catalogue for design quality
